lightPrompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: one distinct OPDA editorial watercolour header illustration for a modelling documentation page.
Composition: a very wide shallow 3:1 panoramic scene, composed horizontally with full meaningful subjects inside the frame and clean open paper around them. Generate one complete illustration, never a collage, grid, screenshot or webpage.
Style: expressive finely detailed organic deep-purple pen-and-ink contours, substantial soft pastel translucent watercolour and softly opaque gouache, visible pigment variation and clean paper highlights. Colourful, warm, humane and refined professional magazine drawing; architectural sketchbook craftsmanship.
Light palette: cool off-white #F9F9F9 paper to the edges, deep purple #231F2F ink, substantial OPDA yellow/gold #FEC92B, petrol/teal #0E8478 and blue-violet #6C5BD4, with supporting rose and coral. No beige or sepia cast.
Constraints: no text, letters, digits, labels, pseudo-writing, signatures, logo, wordmark, watermark or personal information; no photography, 3D, glossy rendering, neon, glow, puzzle pieces, floating icons, handshakes, diagram arrows or generic clipart. Paper documents contain only simple architectural sketches, blank space or flat unlettered colour patches. This is an editorial illustration, not exact evidence or formal notation.
darkPrompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: dark-mode counterpart of an approved OPDA editorial watercolour header.
Input image: the supplied approved light illustration is the EDIT TARGET.
Change ONLY the paper/background, ink values and pigment palette. Preserve the exact subjects and people, identity, count, arrangement, relative sizes, proportions, poses, perspective, framing, crop, negative space and image aspect ratio.
Dark palette: flat deep-purple paper #131224 reaching every edge; rich pastel gold, petrol teal, violet, rose and coral watercolour and softly opaque gouache, with pale lavender and off-white fine ink wherever needed for legibility. Paper must be deep purple, not black, grey or brown. Keep the same calm, colourful, humane magazine illustration.
No redesign, additions, removals, relayout, night scenery, stars, inversion filter, glow, fluorescent outlines, neon, text, labels, signatures or watermarks. This is a palette edit, not a new scene.

export.operation: Whole-image proportional resize, preserving the native source aspect ratio. No crop, forced height, geometry change or CSS inversion. Per-asset quality records any compression adjustment.

pages.title: Review and contribute
pages.prompt: An outdoor community pinup in a modest British residential courtyard, viewed across its full width. Three adult property practitioners stand in a loose informal line studying a long low display rail of individually pinned unlettered house, room and report sketches; one adds a small coral sketch sheet. Gold, petrol and violet clothing; paving, one potted tree and a quiet brick facade establish the outdoor setting. No table, presentation screen, podium, audience rows, voting badges or architectural models. Human practical observations are welcomed; this is not an official approval event.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour of three practitioners adding and comparing property sketches on an outdoor display rail, illustrating different practical observations contributing to a review.

pages.title: Turn experience into a modelling question
pages.prompt: A shallow horizontal view into a quiet real dwelling interior. At one side, a thoughtful adult practitioner holds a simple rectangular paper viewfinder toward the junction between a main room and a small glazed enclosed area. The paper aperture visibly isolates that one room-boundary detail while the larger room remains visible around it. A thin blank sketchpad rests under their arm. Petrol window frames, gold upholstery and coral enclosed-room wall; no report pile, measuring numbers, camera UI, arrows or invented diagram. Focus on narrowing a broad practical problem to one precise distinction.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour of a practitioner using a paper viewfinder to isolate the boundary of an enclosed area while retaining the surrounding room, illustrating a focused modelling question.

pages.title: Review a definition
pages.prompt: A quiet editorial reading corner in shallow three-quarter view. One seated editor studies an open report on an upright wooden reading stand; beside the stand, a separately pinned small watercolour sketch depicts a surveyor visiting a residential doorway. The open report contains a different small architectural sketch and generous entirely blank paper, with a coral removable margin tab. A petrol chair, violet stand and gold pencil create substantial colour. Keep the past visit sketch visibly distinct from the present document review; no text, dates, clock, magnifier, calendar or notebook flat lay. The image suggests asking what the definition actually describes.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour of an editor studying a report on a reading stand beside a separate sketch of a property visit, keeping the document and the event distinguishable.

pages.title: Review a diagram and its relationships
pages.prompt: A physical wall-mounted linen pinboard in a modeller's atelier, seen nearly front-on across a wide shallow composition. Distinct unlettered paper drawings show a whole small building, one separate room, a visit scene and two visibly different report sheets. Thin coloured cotton threads between real brass pins connect several sheets without arrows. A person's single natural hand at the edge gently holds one loose thread near its proper paper endpoint. Coral, petrol, violet and gold paper mounts, delicately sketched linen and realistic physical pin shadows. It must look like tangible material for examining claims, not a formal ontology graph or infographic; no text or node labels.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour of distinct building, room, visit and report sketches on a physical pinboard, with a reviewer tracing one thread between its subjects.

pages.title: Review choices and mappings
pages.prompt: A small architectural specimen display seen obliquely: two separate low fan-shaped stands hold unlettered illustrated door-and-entry panels in different groupings. One stand has three distinct hinged panels, the other a wider overlapping pair. Their petrol, coral and gold entry sketches are recognisable yet not identically interchangeable; a single violet comparison swatch rests in front, and one slim pencil points across the space without touching anything. No people, labels, symbols, arrows, filing drawers or index cards. Tactile painted board, a careful craftsman's collection, showing that plausible choices and groupings deserve comparison rather than assumed equivalence.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour of two separate displays grouping hinged doorway specimens differently, suggesting a careful comparison of the scope of choices.

pages.title: Test a rule with ordinary and difficult cases
pages.prompt: A direct overhead view of a modeller's paper-craft testing mat, laid out as one natural shallow composition rather than a grid. Three distinct miniature room cutouts rest in a loose horizontal row: a simple open room, a room with an enclosed annex, and a room with two separate small obstructed recesses. Loose unlettered translucent coral scope overlays sit partly offset beside them, alongside a teal straightedge and a violet pencil. Substantial gold floors, petrol walls and rose details; visibly tactile thin card edges. No people or full-size inspector, no pass/fail marks, labels, digits, measuring scales, diagram arrows or exact technical plan. Comparing deliberately varied cases is the editorial theme.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour from above of three different paper room cutouts and loose scope overlays, illustrating ordinary and difficult cases used to challenge a proposed rule.

pages.title: Bring evidence others can interpret
pages.prompt: A narrow archive shelving bay in a property office, depicted as a wide horizontal editorial vignette. One careful archivist in a petrol cardigan retrieves a single violet folio from a row of individually wrapped source volumes, opening only its relevant architectural sketch on a nearby shallow shelf. A loose coral interpretation sheet remains separately clipped beside it, not pasted into the original folio. Gold shelf edges and rosy paper tabs, no legible writing anywhere, no filing cabinet UI, stacks of generic blank documents, padlocks or badges. The focal action is finding the specific source while retaining its context and keeping interpretation distinct.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour of an archivist retrieving one architectural source folio from its shelf while keeping a separate interpretation sheet beside it.

pages.title: Read a candidate and compare a change
pages.prompt: A large hinged architectural review portfolio opened across a low sloped stand, alone in a shallow horizontal composition. The left leaf shows one complete modest residential building sketch; the right holds two partially lifted translucent tracing-paper leaves showing the same building with different highlighted room-scope details. Distinct violet and coral tabs identify the separate leaves without any lettering; petrol binding, gold room wash and fine ink are prominent. The underlying building stays consistent; do not depict renovation or demolition. No people, screens, wooden bead graphs, filing drawers or separate house maquette. A physical revision comparison preserving unchanged meaning across views.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour of an opened review portfolio with translucent revision leaves, keeping one building recognisable while highlighting changes in its room descriptions.

pages.title: Follow feedback, disagreement and revision
pages.prompt: A low wall rail in an intimate review alcove holds several separate property sketch revisions on brass bulldog clips. Two adult reviewers stand at opposite ends of the wide rail; one gently places a new coral note alongside an earlier violet sketch, while the other points to a still-unresolved small petrol detail. A clearly separate final blank patch leaves space for the remaining question. The sketches depict room scope and report outline, not text. Warm human attention, gold clip detail, no celebratory pose, checkmark, vote, approval stamp, long table, timeline arrows or process diagram. The scene is revisiting a reasoned conversation, not announcing a completed release.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour of two reviewers revisiting separately clipped property sketches, adding a note while keeping an unresolved detail visible.

pages.title: Connect meanings across contexts
pages.prompt: An architectural cutaway across two established neighbouring workshop rooms, one petrol and one violet, each with its own distinctive unlettered sketches and drawing materials. A fixed wall clearly preserves their separate spaces, with one small shared service hatch through which two people compare a coral document while leaving their different local drawings in their own room. Gold details warm the connected threshold. Wide low frontal perspective, no bridge, river, floating maps or discovery/exploration scene. This is an editorial metaphor for accountable semantic homes communicating without merging, not a literal map of OPDA contexts.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour cutaway of two distinct workshop rooms whose occupants compare one document through a shared hatch while retaining their separate drawings.

pages.title: Rules, requirements and exceptions
pages.prompt: An inviting wide illustration of an older Black male reader with short silver hair seated on a low violet bench, holding an open architectural report with entirely unlettered sketch panels. Beside the reader is a single gold miniature doorway frame with a removable coral scope screen partly slid out, and a separate small blank checklist strip that is not ticked. A petrol pencil pauses above the relevant sketch before any judgement. Shallow full-scene view with a quiet paper background; no other people, room cutout collection, pass/fail badges, computer, tables of outcomes, labels, letters or digits. The careful pause asks whether a requirement applies before checking the detail.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour of a reader pausing over an architectural report beside a doorway model with a movable scope screen, illustrating the need to establish applicability before judging a requirement.

pages.title: Sensitivity, purpose and permissions
pages.prompt: A private reading-room vignette from a shallow elevated angle: one older East Asian woman with short silver hair in a petrol chair reads a single narrow architectural extract on a small sloped lectern, while a substantial violet folding privacy screen covers the rest of a longer document behind it. Only the selected coral-edged extract is visible; a gold paper marker and a plain small closed folio sit separately within reach. Show an intentional limited view, not a security appliance or enforced permission system. No padlocks, shield icons, gates, badges, identity cards, login screens, text, letters, numbers or visible personal information. Rich pastel paper surfaces, calm considerate human scale.
pages.alt: Pastel watercolour of a person reading one selected architectural extract while a folding screen keeps the rest of the material covered, illustrating information scope rather than an access grant.
